title: Card details entered on a parcel-delivery scam, on the work laptop

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: I think I have been scammed

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
I had a text saying a parcel needed a redelivery fee. I opened it on the work
laptop and paid the 1.99 with my own debit card, number
4539 8721 0034 6612. I realised about ten minutes later when the page asked
for my bank password as well, which I did not give.

It is my own card, not a company one. Do I need to do anything about the
laptop?

Mel

handling.escalation_reason: A phishing site was opened on a company laptop and details were entered; somebody has to decide what the laptop needs.

must_not_appear.why: a payment card number, which must not reach a model or be repeated back

rationale: The pair with case-039, and the difference is the point. There a work password went into a phishing page, which is a credential compromise and P1. Here what was given was her own card and no work credential, so nothing of the company's is exposed and the priority is P2 - but a phishing page was opened on a managed laptop, which is still security-sensitive under G3 and still a person's call. A reviewer who reads the prompt's 'confirmed phishing click' as P1 regardless of what was entered would be reading it literally, and that disagreement is worth having on the record. The card number is the scrubbing test (G8).
